title: BenchLab snapshot and scheduler hypothesis list
body:
Purpose and quick context:
This is a working snapshot from the BenchLab cluster after the 2025-02 throughput regressions. Goal: capture exact microbench configs, a prioritized list of scheduler/KV-cache hypotheses, and a minimal reproducer we can share with infra and kernel teams. This is deliberately informal — think of it as a lab notebook + action checklist.

Recent incident summary (short):
- Date window: 2025-02-10 -> 2025-02-15
- Symptom: 3–4x p95 token latency increase for short-chat workloads (seq len ~128) during high concurrency bursts; throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~25% under steady state for mixed small/long workloads.
- Impacted variants: grouped-limited scheduler (v2.3), kernel-fallback path (int8), and workloads with heavy KV churn.
- First detection: alerting on p95 SLO slack + client-reported timeouts.

BenchLab snapshot (what I ran locally on benchlab-03):
- commit/tag: benchlab/2025-02-13-snapshot (SHA: a1c9f3e)
- binary: serve-runtime v0.52.1 (debug build) with scheduler feature flags enabled
- hardware: 4x A100-80GB in homogeneous pool (driver: 535.86), NVMe swap disabled
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04
- microbench harness: benchit v0.9.3 (config inline below)

Minimal harness config (notes-to-self):
- worker threads: 32
- batch window ms: 10
- max batch tokens: 8192
- kv-cache size: 1.5M entries; eviction: LRU-approx
- scheduler mode: grouped-limited (concurrency cap = 64), fast-path favor small sequences = true
- trace sampling: headroom 0.02, full traces on anomalies
- synthetic workload: 80% chat-short (prompt tokens 100, response cap 50), 20% chat-long (prompt 900, response cap 300)

Observed micro-metrics (averages from 30m run):
- aggregate tokens/s: 1.9M (expected baseline: 2.5M)
- p50 token latency: 4.1ms (baseline: 3.8ms)
- p95 token latency: 42ms (baseline: 12ms)
- KV hit-rate overall: 61% (baseline: ~78%)
- scheduler queue depth (avg): 120
- kernel fallback rate (int8->fp16 path): 0.8% of batches (spikes to 7% during bursts)

Light-weight trace observations (samples):
- trace A (burst start): many short requests get coalesced, then a sudden spike in long requests; scheduler moves long requests to tail and attempts to keep small-first policy -> queue depth climbs; KV cache churn spikes as long requests repopulate large prefix caches -> eviction increases -> hit-rate falls -> backend kernel path sees more cold cache, causing more kernel fallback for int8 quant path (observed extra kernel instantiation delays ~1.2ms each).
- trace B (steady state): throughput lower than expected while GPU utilization was moderate (60-70%). Suspicion: scheduler backpressure plus excessive KV-cache maintenance lock contention.

Hypothesis list (prioritized):
1) Scheduler fairness edge-case: grouped-limited's small-first heuristics starve fair scheduling when request size mix varies quickly -> long-tail queueing and increased latency. (Evidence: queue depth & trace A)
2) KV-cache lock contention: our CRC-based eviction + global metadata lock causes stalls when many long requests repopulate large prefixes, amplifying latency under bursty long-request arrivals. (Evidence: increased eviction rate and observed lock hold times in microtrace)
3) Kernel path thrashing for quantized operators: fallback from int8 to fp16 due to cold KV state results in extra kernel start-ups; combined with batch reshaping leads to throughput loss. (Evidence: fallback rate spikes correlated with KV hit-rate drops)
4) Batching window tuning: current 10ms window may be combining incompatible sequences under mixed workloads causing suboptimal kernel selection and memory layout fragmentation. (Evidence: p95 improves when lowering window to 4ms in quick A/B)
5) Runtime GC or bookkeeping jitter: periodic maintenance tasks (cache compaction) run at 30s interval and coincide with observed p95 spikes. (Evidence: some spikes align with compaction timestamps from benchlab logs)

Test matrix (cheap first):
- T1: disable small-first heuristic in grouped-limited schedule (A/B for 30m) -> measure p95, queue depth, KV hit-rate.
- T2: switch KV eviction to sharded LRU (4 shards) to reduce lock contention -> 1h run.
- T3: reduce batch window to 4ms, keep other flags -> 1h run.
- T4: force int8-only kernel fallback off (fail closed -> error rather than fallback) on a canary pool to confirm fallback costs -> short run under sampled traffic.
- T5: stagger cache compaction schedule (randomize offsets) to test compaction correlation -> 2h run.

Preliminary results (ran T1/T3 on benchlab-03):
- T1 (disable small-first): p95 down to 18ms (from 42ms); queue depth avg 68; KV hit-rate still 62% -> suggests scheduler policy heavily influences queueing. However small request p50 increased slightly (4.8ms) indicating some fairness trade-off.
- T3 (4ms window): tokens/s recovered to 2.25M; p95 22ms; KV hit-rate improved marginally to 65% -> better kernel packing and less memory fragmentation.
- Caveat: both changes reduced p95 but didn't restore baseline; KV hit-rate remains low, so KV contention likely contributes to residual gap.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Marco: run T2 (sharded LRU) on benchlab-02 and benchlab-03; include traces and lock-hold histograms. ETA: 2025-03-05.
- Sophie: instrument KV metadata lock to export per-shard histograms and average hold times to Grafana. ETA: 2025-03-04.
- Evan: build a canary with int8 fallback disabled and run T4 on canary pool under sampled traffic (20% load). ETA: 2025-03-06.
- Aisha: run a 6h mixed workload with T1+T2+T3 combined on benchlab-01 to measure end-to-end interactions; capture full traces. ETA: 2025-03-10.

Reproducer steps (minimal):
1) Checkout benchlab snapshot: git checkout a1c9f3e && make bench-image
2) Deploy to benchlab-03 with flags: --scheduler=grouped-limited --small-first=true --batch-window-ms=10 --kv-shards=1
3) Start benchit with workload profile short-heavy.json (attached in linked artifacts)
4) Enable trace sampling; after 10m collect traces in /var/log/benchlab/traces

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- Does sharded eviction impact memory overhead in ways that hurt kernel tiling decisions? Need to profile memory layouts.
- Can we make KV repopulation async to avoid blocking critical fast-path threads? Prototype idea: mark repopulation as low-priority work queued to background threads.
- Consider adding a lightweight admission control for long requests during burst windows (reject or queue to lower-priority pool). Trade-offs with SLA — product needs to weigh.

Next steps for doc:
- Convert these lab notes into an RFC if T2 shows measurable lock contention reduction.
- Draft a short customer-facing postmortem template if we confirm root cause.
- Add collected traces and microbench configs to Confluence page linked above.

Appendix (quick commands & artifacts):
- reproducer command: ./benchit --config configs/short-heavy.json --rps 1200 --duration 3600 --traces on
- quick grep for fallback events: rg "kernel fallback" /var/log/serve/*.log
- profiler snapshot path: /opt/benchlab/profiles/2025-02-14-15z

Notes (random):
- I threw in the 'small-first' test because similar behavior showed up in a customer incident last year; happy we have a cheap A/B that moved the needle.
- For the RFC: avoid prescriptive fixes early, present trade-offs (throughput vs p95 fairness vs implementation complexity).

End of snapshot. Keep this doc lightweight and iterate — I'll update after T2/T4 results.
